next_step: Finalize dedicated commit level, confirm burst and overage terms, legal review of DPA.
notes:
Background:
- Mid-market product analytics vendor building chat and semantic surfaces across product and support.
- Ran 6-week Hosted API POC (Nov–Dec 2025): ~120k chat interactions, embeddings for search across 3M documents.

POC outcomes / technical summary:
- Latency targets: P50 <150ms, P95 <300ms for short-turn chat (satisfied on Hosted API for baseline traffic).
- Throughput target for launch: 40-60 RPS applied across chat endpoints; expected peak concurrency 120 sessions.
- Embeddings pipeline: batch 2M documents monthly, embed/update cadence nightly.
- Model preference: open-ish Llama-family / 70B class OK; willing to accept quantized variants if quality holds.

Current commercial conversation (Dedicated):
- Use-case: move to Dedicated for predictable cost and data isolation (customer data never stored in multi-tenant cache).
- Redwood quote requested for committed nodes + burst: initial commit = 2 reserved GPU nodes (prod), ramp to 4 nodes @ month 3, 6 nodes @ month 6.
- Burst: allow +150% capacity for up to 48 hours (for event-driven spikes). Need per-minute burst billing & clear reconciliation.
- Overage: EmberPort wants a clear overage rate cap; target <= $0.30 per 1k tokens (negotiation point).
- Pricing ask: sliding commit discount milestones at 3/6/12 months; EmberPort expects ~25-35% discount off list for 12-month commit at target ARR.
- Ramp schedule being used to structure contract: month 0-2 (2 nodes), month 3-5 (+2 nodes), month 6 onward (+2 nodes).
- Private/VPC requirement: control plane via Redwood Private for audit logs; but initial deployment still in Redwood Dedicated in customer VPC.

Procurement & internal stakeholders:
- Champion: VP Product (Amir Rao) — cares about SLOs and quality regressions.
- Infrastructure lead: Rachel Ng — owns deployment/VPC constraints and KMS integration.
- Finance: CFO (Ellen Park) wants cost model comparison vs continued Hosted spend; needs final PO signed by Apr 15.
- Legal: reviewing DPA/data residency clause; flagged points around retention and subprocessor list.

Recent timeline (CRM snippets):
- 2026-02-03: Hosted POC wrap call; engineering happy with latency; asked for Dedicated price examples (Fireflies ff-3221).
- 2026-02-18: Deep dive w/ SE (Liam) on autoscale/queueing behavior; requested benchmarking on 70B quantized model.

Quotes / direct notes from calls:
- Amir (VP Product): "We need predictable monthly cost or we can't commit — bursts are OK but reconcile into a clear monthly spend model."
- Rachel (Infra): "KMS + per-region residency are must-haves; no cross-region KV cache sharing."
- Ellen (CFO): "If the Dedicated path increases our run-rate by >2.5x vs hosted, we can't approve without measurable cost offsets."

Open items to close before PO:
- Finalized committed node counts and monthly prices for each ramp milestone (teams want a flat monthly committed fee + usage overage model).
- Precise burst billing model (per-minute billing, reconciliation to committed usage, max burst budget).
- Overage rate cap and treatment of cached tokens (do cached hits count? definition needed).
- Legal signoff on DPA and data residency; need Redwood security to provide SOC2 + subprocessor list (requested).

Next steps (short):

- SE (Liam) to deliver quantized benchmark numbers for 70B model on Dedicated by 2026-03-18.
- Legal to respond to DPA redlines; ask security for SOC2 attestation and subprocessor list.
- CFO deadline: PO decision week of 2026-04-13 — aim to have final commercial terms by 2026-04-06.

CRM-style quick summary (for AE notes):

- Price sensitivity high; target ARR 150k-300k but only with favorable commit discount and clear overage cap.
- Decision timeline tight: legal + finance gating; AE should push pricing term sheet and obligation schedule ASAP.
